title: Normalized locally closed extension on module sheaves

from.place: Proof (2), the module-sheaf construction underlying composition of immersion extensions; Steps 1--9 of lem-sfb-locally-closed-extension-coherence.

statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme (locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]), and let $R$ be an arbitrary sheaf of commutative rings on its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and inverse-image coefficient identifications [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. There is a simultaneous system of exact extension functors $a_!$ for locally closed immersions $a:S\hookrightarrow X$ (closed followed by open [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion]), allowing any source coefficient sheaf identified with $a^{-1}R$. For open $a$, $a_!$ is left adjoint to actual module inverse image $a^*$, with invertible unit; equivalently it is the extension presheaf [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf] followed by module sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] on the open slice site. For closed $a$, there is an isomorphism $a_!\cong a_*$ to actual module direct image. There are natural isomorphisms $r_a:a^*a_!\cong1$, equal for open $a$ to the inverse unit and for closed $a$ to the actual inverse-image/direct-image counit after this comparison. For composable locally closed immersions $b:T\hookrightarrow S$ and $a:S\hookrightarrow X$ there are natural isomorphisms $\gamma_{a,b}:a_!b_!\cong(ab)_!$ which restrict to the identity under $r_a,r_b,r_{ab}$ and the canonical inverse-image composition comparison. There are identity comparisons $(1_X)_!\cong1$, and these comparisons satisfy both unit laws and the associativity law, after the canonical equalities of composite coefficient immersions. Consequently both factorization orders give the same normalized extension, independent of factorization. This assertion concerns module sheaves; it makes no assertion about derived categories.

proof.text: Construct the fixed closed-then-open model for every coefficient immersion. Its additive, finite-limit, finite-colimit, full and faithful instances and modelRestriction are proved from the actual open and closed adjunctions. Coefficient parameter definitions are reexported unchanged from the data module.

For each immersion use the boundary lemma to obtain the normalized open adjunction and the normalized actual closed comparison. These supply exactly the open and closed fields of LocallyClosedExtensionData.

For each pair and input module take the objectwise binary isomorphism. Full faithfulness and modelRestriction prove that a normalized map is unique. The generic normalizedNatIso argument proves naturality: apply restriction to the naturality square, postcompose with modelRestriction, and use naturality of both restriction comparisons. Restriction is injective on morphisms from an object isomorphic to an extension image. Thus these objectwise comparisons form gamma with exactly the required binary normalization.

Apply the conditional unit/associativity theorem to this normalized natural gamma. Assemble the extension, exactness, restriction, open and closed comparisons, gamma and identity into LocallyClosedExtensionData. Its NormalizedComposition fields are respectively the proved binary normalization and the three returned coherence equations.

proof_origin.place: Fixed model and categorical assembly of Steps 1--9, with boundary, objectwise binary existence, and formal unit/associativity left as three strictly smaller statements.
